hn.originalTitle: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Comment 1: > Is it public? > > Search your GitHub organization for .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json. Each hit is a file anyone can read right now. So, it's not necessarily "public", it's simply in the repository, and whether it's actually public or not depends on the repository settings. Or am I missing something

Comment 2: Thanks, fair point. Our 1,122 files are all in public repos. In a private repo, only people with access can read it, but "don't ask again" still writes the password into a project file that gets committed, so it spreads with every clone and fork, and goes public if the repo does.

Comment 3: > So, it's not necessarily "public", it's simply in the repository, and whether it's actually public or not depends on the repository settings. Even then, you might not want every developer in your company to have the password to the production SQL database...

Comment 4: Confusing headline. They scanned for repos where people had committed their .claude/ folder and local settings and then scanned those files for commands which contained keys or passwords. So pressing “Don’t Ask Again” by itself doesn’t expose passwords by itself. If you commit your local Claude settings and in those settings you have manually approved commands containing secrets directly in the command and then you publish the repo, that’s exposed.
hn.titleZh: Claude Code 的「Don’t Ask Again」揭露了 1,122 個公開 GitHub 文件中的密碼
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Claude 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh: 評論1： > 公開嗎？ >> 在您的 GitHub 組織中搜尋 .claude/settings.local.json 和 .claude/settings.json。每個點擊都是任何人現在都可以讀取的檔案。因此，它不一定是“公開的”，它只是在存儲庫中，並且它是否實際上是公開的取決於存儲庫設定。或者我錯過了什麼評論2：謝謝，公平的觀點。我們的 1,122 個文件都在公共倉庫中。在私人儲存庫中，只有具有存取權限的人才能讀取它，但「不再詢問」仍然會將密碼寫入提交的專案文件中，因此它會隨著每個克隆和分叉而傳播，並且如果存儲庫這樣做，它也會公開。評論3：> 所以，它不一定是“公開的”，它只是在儲存庫中，而它是否真正公開取決於儲存庫設定。即使如此，您可能也不希望公司中的每個開發人員都擁有生產 SQL 資料庫的密碼... 評論 4：令人困惑的標題。他們掃描人們提交了 .claude/ 資料夾和本地設定的儲存庫，然後掃描這些檔案以查找包含密鑰或密碼的命令。因此，按下「不要再詢問」本身並不會暴露密碼。如果您提交本地 Claude 設置，並且在這些設置中您手動批准了直接在命令中包含機密的命令，然後發布了存儲庫，那麼該存儲庫就會暴露。

hn.originalTitle: AI agents stole 190k gaming credentials for under $400 in model costs
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns - Check Point Research

Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns - Check Point Research CATEGORIES AI Research 23

Android Malware 23

Artificial Intelligence 5

Check Point Research Publications 480

Data & Threat Intelligence 2

Global Cyber Attack Reports 432

Russo-Ukrainian War 1

Threat and data analysis 0

Threat Research 175

Web 3.0 Security 11

Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns

Agentic hacking platforms like ARTEX, where AI models autonomously drive vulnerability discovery and exploitation, have been observed to be used by various cyber criminals.

Check Point Research’s analysis of the current landscape observed more than 1,800 publicly exposed instances for ARTEX alone , showing a massive scale of deployments.

While previous threat reports on ARTEX focused on the observed telemetry on the victim side, we present artifacts from the operator consoles . This data shows which models were used as well as how the operators prompted their agents.

Most attacks were fully autonomous besides the initial goal setup. Threat actors barely interacted with their agent fleets.

In the observed activity, Chinese models are most prevalent , with Deepseek Flash taking the lead. Operators mostly only interacted with their agents to check the progress of the current operations – attacks were almost fully autonomous .

The goals set by the attackers were exclusively to carry out opportunistic, financially motivated cybercrime , mostly on a broad scale. Agents abused various web vulnerabilities, such as Remote Code Execution (RCE), to achieve their goals. In some cases, agents were using the access gained to actively carry out supply chain attacks.

ARTEX is a Chinese open-source, AI-powered penetration testing platform designed to help security teams assess systems they own or are authorized to test. It uses large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multiple AI agents that plan tests, run security tools, and record evidence of potential vulnerabilities. Its web dashboard brings together assets, testing progress, captured traffic, and findings, allowing users to monitor activity and guide the agents. By linking each investigation to specific assets and supporting vulnerability retesting, ARTEX aims to reduce repetitive work while keeping human oversight central to the testing process.

After the tool was observed in attacks against South Korean banks , its developer decided to make the project closed-source on October 8th. However, various maintained forks and backups of the original repository keep the tool publicly available to threat actors.

As described further below, artifacts obtained by Check Point Research show that these systems can work fully autonomously after the initial goal has been set by the operator. Using agentic hacking frameworks like ARTEX, threat actors can carry out attacks at a previously impossible speed, on a broad scale and without any technical knowledge, opening the field to a large set of people.

Besides ARTEX, other frameworks such as CyberStrike , Cairn or PentAGI offer similar capabilities. Check Point Research also observed various other custom agentic hacking frameworks in the wild. While some of these are based on open-source tools such as those mentioned above, others are written from the ground up.

While many ARTEX instances are hidden behind firewalls or are set up in local networks, threat actors often expose administrative interfaces to the internet, to make them accessible remotely. Check Point Research found 2,557 systems hosting or having hosted ARTEX panels, with 1,608 live and publicly available instances at the time of the research. A metadata analysis of these servers gives valuable insights into the distribution and usage.

Additionally, 10 instances were misconfigured to expose the full ARTEX database – giving a rare insight into how actors prompted their agents, which models were used and the exact steps and attacks the agents carried out.

In the analyzed 10 instances, Chinese models dominate the share of configured LLMs, with models of the Deepseek Flash family being the most prevalent. With American models configured on 3 different instances, we observed guardrails being hit only when using Anthropic’s Opus 5.5. Here, the actor subsequently switched to more permissive Chinese models.

hn.sourceTextZh:
自動駕駛儀駭客攻擊：ARTEX 網路犯罪活動內部 - Check Point 研究 自動駕駛儀駭客攻擊：ARTEX 網路犯罪活動內部 - Check Point 研究 類別 人工智慧研究 23 Android 惡意軟體 23 人工智慧 5 Check Point 研究出版品 480 資料和威脅情報 2 全球網路攻擊報告 432 俄羅斯- 107 威脅 107 威脅 1075 310 32 Autopilot 上的駭客攻擊：ARTEX 網路犯罪活動內部 像 ARTEX 這樣的代理駭客平台（其中人工智慧模型自動驅動漏洞發現和利用）已被各種網路犯罪分子使用。 Check Point Research 對目前情勢的分析觀察到，僅 ARTEX 一項公開暴露的實例就超過 1,800 個，顯示出大規模的部署。雖然先前關於 ARTEX 的威脅報告著重於在受害者一側觀察到的遙測數據，但我們展示了來自操作員控制台的工件。這些數據顯示了使用了哪些模型以及運營商如何提示他們的代理商。除了最初的目標設定之外，大多數攻擊都是完全自主的。威脅行為者幾乎不與他們的特工艦隊互動。在觀察到的活動中，中國模型最為普遍，其中 Deepseek Flash 處於領先地位。

操作员大多只与他们的代理进行交互来检查当前操作的进度——攻击几乎是完全自主的。攻擊者設定的目標完全是為了實施機會主義的、出於經濟動機的網路犯罪，而且大多是大規模的。特工濫用各種網路漏洞，例如遠端執行程式碼（RCE）來實現他們的目標。在某些情況下，特工利用所獲得的存取權限主動發動供應鏈攻擊。 ARTEX 是一個由中國開源、人工智慧驅動的滲透測試平台，旨在幫助安全團隊評估他們擁有或有權測試的系統。它使用大型语言模型 (LLM) 来协调多个 AI 代理，以计划测试、运行安全工具并记录潜在漏洞的证据。其網路儀表板匯集了資產、測試進度、捕獲的流量和結果，允許使用者監控活動並指導代理商。透過將每次調查與特定資產聯繫起來並支援漏洞重新測試，ARTEX 旨在減少重複性工作，同時將人類監督作為測試過程的核心。在該工具在針對韓國銀行的攻擊中被發現後，其開發者決定在 10 月 8 日關閉該專案的原始程式碼。然而，原始儲存庫的各種維護的分叉和備份使威脅行為者可以公開使用該工具。

如下文進一步所述，Check Point Research 獲得的工件表明，在操作員設定初始目標後，這些系統可以完全自主地工作。使用 ARTEX 等代理駭客框架，威脅行為者可以以前所未有的速度、大範圍、無需任何技術知識的情況下實施攻擊，從而向大量人員開放該領域。除了 ARTEX 之外，其他框架（例如 Cyber​​Strike、Cairn 或 PentAGI）也提供類似的功能。 Check Point Research 也觀察了各種其他自訂代理程式駭客框架。雖然其中一些是基於如上所述的開源工具，但其他一些是從頭開始編寫的。雖然許多 ARTEX 實例隱藏在防火牆後面或設定在本地網路中，但威脅行為者經常將管理介面暴露到互聯網，以便遠端存取它們。 Check Point Research 發現 2,557 個系統託管或已經託管 ARTEX 面板，在研究時有 1,608 個即時和公開可用的實例。對這些伺服器的元資料分析可以提供有關分佈和使用情況的寶貴見解。此外，10 個實例配置錯誤，暴露了完整的 ARTEX 資料庫，從而讓我們能夠罕見地了解攻擊者如何提示其代理、使用了哪些模型以及代理執行的確切步驟和攻擊。

在分析的 10 個實例中，中國模型在配置的法學碩士中佔據主導地位，其中 Deepseek Flash 系列模型最為普遍。在 3 個不同實例上配置的美國模型中，我們觀察到只有在使用 Anthropic 的 Opus 5.5 時才會撞到護欄。在這裡，這位演員隨後轉向了更寬容的中國模特兒。觀察到的活動 這些活動針對各行業，目標包括取得加密貨幣、竊取程式碼簽章憑證或玩弄加密貨幣等。

hn.originalTitle: Ask HN: What hardware are you using to run local LLMs?
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Figured I'd ask here because I have no doubt some of you are running some pretty cool, cost effective solutions for local models. Don't doubt some have mini data centers in their closets either haha, but just looking to get a view into what fellow HN'ers are using for their day to day work.

Comment 1: I have a 3090 w/ 24G VRAM, it supports flash attention and bf16, but is a bit old. I dont run generative models on it as they would be slow and inaccurate, but I do run embedding models, OCR, and system one (decision) models on it.

Comment 2: I got pretty good results with my 3090 on Qwen 27b. Yeah, the rack is completely unusable when you launch the llm, but i wouldn't say its slow. Btw, fellow 3090 user, some time ago i saw this: https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock Can't try it personally because windows, but maybe it will help you.

Comment 3: OK, that gpu-unlock is something I've never seen before and...wow. I did some research and NVidia really did kneecap their RTX for market segmentation. Grrrrr

Comment 4: Wow, this seems to speed up inference by 68% or something for me. Holy shit.

hn.sourceTextZh: 我想我會在這裡問，因為我毫不懷疑你們中的一些人正在為本地模型運行一些非常酷的、具有成本效益的解決方案。不要懷疑有些人的衣櫃裡有迷你資料中心，哈哈，但只是想了解一下 HN 的同事在日常工作中使用什麼。評論 1：我有一個 3090 w/ 24G VRAM，它支援 Flash Attention 和 bf16，但有點舊。我不會在其上運行生成模型，因為它們會很慢且不準確，但我會在其上運行嵌入模型、OCR 和系統一（決策）模型。評論 2：我的 3090 在 Qwen 27b 上得到了相當不錯的結果。是的，當你啟動 llm 時，機架完全無法使用，但我不會說它很慢。順便說一句，3090 用戶，前段時間我看到了這個：https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock 由於 Windows 無法親自嘗試，但也許它會對你有所幫助。評論 3：好的，GPU 解鎖是我以前從未見過的東西......哇。我做了一些研究，NVidia 確實對 RTX 進行了市場區隔。 Grrrrr 評論 4：哇，這似乎將推理速度加快了 68%，對我來說還是這樣。天啊。

hn.sourceOriginalText:
Comment 1: Both Anthropic and OpenAI seem to delay their new models until the other company releases. I guess this will stop after the Anthropic IPO.

Comment 2: I strongly suspect they are "pacing the frontier", maybe not explicitly in cooperation, but the models are now at a point where cracks in alignment could seriously blow up in the labs face. We can only imagine the backlash to "High school kid brings Bank of America to it's knees for 7 hours with ChatGPT hack" The "plateau" of LLMs could turn out to be the "plateau" of publically available LLMs.

Comment 3: Haven’t found a convincing argument to why they would continue to release models under the assumption of being on an exponential. So hard agree

Comment 4: Certainly a big topic. In terms of Fable 5.5 at least it seems not to be the case, because partners already have access to it for 2 weeks. I consider it likely they are afraid of timing in regards to the GPT 6.2 release and government intervention risks related to IPO. (like last time).

hn.originalTitle: AI agents hallucinate prices: LLM grounding with live data
hn.sourceOriginalText:
LLM grounding tutorial: stop AI agents guessing prices

Ask an AI agent with no tools what a Kindle Paperwhite costs, and it can answer $159.99, the old launch price. The live price at the time of testing was $199.99. In tests, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 each matched the live price exactly for 2 of 15 products from memory. With built-in web search, they gave more exact prices, but every run still had wrong prices, each with a source link.

Large language model (LLM) grounding is the standard way to stop both kinds of wrong price, from memory and from web search. A grounded agent answers only from data that it fetched for the question, and every answer shows where that data came from. For prices, a grounded agent needs live data, a clear status when a check fails, and code, not the model, that writes each price into the answer.

The Python agent below has each of these. It gets live prices from E-commerce Scraping Tool , a ready-to-run tool on the Apify marketplace. Apify calls these tools Actors. First, the tests show where wrong prices come from. Then you build the agent and test it step by step.

Why AI agents hallucinate prices

If your agent shows prices, a wrong one can reach your user in 3 main ways. The model answers from memory, it reads a bad page, or a tool says "ok" when it failed. The tests below check the first 2, on 21 live product pages from Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and 4 Shopify stores. A research study tests the third.

The live prices come from E-commerce Scraping Tool, and an independent check with a separate scraping service, from US IP addresses, matched the Actor on all 21 pages. The results include only the 15 products with a single clear price for a new item, as a US shopper sees it without member discounts or coupons. A price is exact only when it matches the live price to the cent. The other 6 pages showed no price, or an unclear seller or size. The 15 prices didn't change while the models answered.

An LLM learns prices during training, and many of those prices change before a user asks. With no tools, gpt-6-luna and Claude Opus 5.5 gave these results. The last row adds the prompt "If you cannot know the current price, answer UNKNOWN":

Without the UNKNOWN prompt, Claude Opus 5.5 added a clear warning, such as "I can't check live prices," to all 21 answers. Each answer still included a price, and agent code reads the number, not the warning. So a prompt alone gave the user either a guess or nothing.

Prices can also change fast. The AirPods Pro 3 at Best Buy went from $199.99 to $249.99 in the 3 days before the models were asked. Even a price from last week can mislead your user.

When your agent fetches pages itself, the page can be the wrong one, even when it loads normally.

Wrong country. A request from outside the US received an Amazon page in Indian rupees. The model read it correctly and answered INR 7,503.02 for an Instant Pot that cost $79 in the US.

Wrong seller. An Amazon page showed "No featured offers available." The model answered $71.89. That price came from the line "Other sellers on Amazon New & Used (2) from $71.89," not from the Buy Box, the main offer on an Amazon page.

Wrong variant. Target redirected the link for the black Kindle Paperwhite to its parent product page, and Owala redirected its FreeSip link to the 32 oz size. A price from the new page can belong to another variant.

Code can detect each of these cases, because the data shows the currency, the seller, and the final page URL.

From a tool that says "ok" when it failed

The preprint Fabrication after tool failure , a study shared before peer review, tested what models do when a tool returns bad data. When the tool returned "ok" with bad data, such as an empty, outdated, or incomplete result, up to 45.3% of answers were dishonest. A dishonest answer hid the failure. When the tool returned an error status instead, the study reported 0% dishonest answers. So a price tool that reports a clear status or error helps the agent give honest answers.

What the 3 causes have in common

In all 3 causes, the wrong price looks like a normal answer, and nothing tells the user that something failed. The scraper tests show this. In 3 test runs, a simple do-it-yourself (DIY) scraper received 26 block pages. A block page is what a store shows when it blocks a request, such as Walmart's "Robot or human?" page or Amazon's "Continue shopping" page. The model answered "no price" for all 26. Those answers were honest, but the user still got no price. Every clearly wrong
hn.titleZh: 人工智慧代理產生幻覺價格：法學碩士以即時數據為基礎
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 LLM / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
LLM 基礎教學：阻止 AI 代理猜測價格 問一個沒有工具的 AI 代理 Kindle Paperwhite 的價格是多少，它可以回答 159.99 美元，即舊的發布價格。測試時的即時價格為 199.99 美元。在測試中，GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 均與記憶體中 15 個產品中的 2 個的即時價格完全匹配。透過內建的網路搜索，他們給出了更準確的價格，但每次運行仍然有錯誤的價格，每個價格都有一個來源連結。大語言模型 (LLM) 基礎是阻止記憶和網路搜尋中兩種錯誤價格的標準方法。接地代理僅根據為問題獲取的數據進行回答，並且每個答案都會顯示該數據的來源。對於價格，接地代理需要即時資料、檢查失敗時的清晰狀態，以及將每個價格寫入答案的程式碼（而不是模型）。下面的 Python 代理程式具有其中的每一個。它從 E-commerce Scraping Tool 獲取實時價格，E-commerce Scraping Tool 是 Apify 市場上的一個可立即運行的工具。 Apify 將這些工具稱為 Actor。首先，測試顯示錯誤的價格從何而來。然後您建立代理並逐步測試它。為什麼人工智慧代理會產生幻覺如果您的代理顯示價格，錯誤的價格可能會透過 3 種主要方式到達您的用戶。模型根據記憶進行回答，它讀取了錯誤的頁面，或者工具在失敗時說“正常”。

下面的测试检查前 2 个，即来自 Amazon、Walmart、Best Buy、Target 和 4 个 Shopify 商店的 21 个实时产品页面。一项研究测试了第三个。即時價格來自電子商務抓取工具，並使用單獨的抓取服務進行的獨立檢查來自美國 IP 位址，與所有 21 個頁面上的演員相符。结果仅包括 15 种新产品具有单一明确价格的产品，正如美国购物者所看到的，没有会员折扣或优惠券。仅当实时价格与美分相符时，价格才是准确的。其他 6 页没有显示价格，或者不清楚的卖家或尺寸。 15款价格没有变化，但型号有回应。法学硕士在培训期间了解价格，其中许多价格在用户询问之前就发生了变化。在没有工具的情况下，gpt-6-luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 给出了这些结果。最後一行添加了提示「如果您無法知道當前價格，請回答 UNKNOWN」：在沒有 UNKNOWN 提示的情況下，Claude Opus 5.5 對所有 21 個答案添加了明確的警告，例如「我無法檢查實時價格」。每个答案仍然包含价格，代理代码读取的是数字，而不是警告。因此，单独的提示要么给用户一个猜测，要么什么也没有。价格也可能变化很快。在询问型号之前的 3 天内，百思买的 AirPods Pro 3 从 199.99 美元涨到了 249.99 美元。即使是上周的价格也可能会误导您的用户。

當您的代理商自行取得頁面時，該頁面可能是錯誤的，即使它正常載入也是如此。錯誤的國家。來自美國境外的請求收到了以印度盧比顯示的亞馬遜頁面。該模型正確讀取並回答了速溶鍋的價格為 7,503.02 印度盧比，在美國售價為 79 美元。錯誤的賣家。亞馬遜頁面顯示「沒有可用的特色優惠」。該模特兒的回答為 71.89 美元。該價格來自「亞馬遜上的其他賣家全新和二手 (2) 起價 71.89 美元」這一行，而不是來自亞馬遜頁面上的主要報價「Buy Box」。錯誤的變體。 Target 將黑色 Kindle Paperwhite 的連結重定向到其父產品頁面，Owala 將其 FreeSip 連結重定向到 32 盎司尺寸。新頁面中的價格可以屬於另一個變體。程式碼可以偵測每種情況，因為數據顯示了貨幣、賣家和最終頁面 URL。工具失敗後說「ok」的工具 工具失敗後的預印本 Fabrication 是一項在同行評審之前分享的研究，測試了當工具傳回錯誤資料時模型會做什麼。當工具傳回「正常」且資料錯誤（例如結果為空、過時或不完整）時，高達 45.3% 的答案是不誠實的。不誠實的回答掩蓋了失敗。相反，當工具傳回錯誤狀態時，研究報告不誠實答案的比例為 0%。因此，報告明確狀態或錯誤的價格工具可以幫助代理商給出誠實的答案。

這 3 個原因的共同點 在所有 3 個原因中，錯誤的價格看起來像是正常的答案，並且沒有任何資訊告訴用戶某些事情失敗了。刮刀測試表明了這一點。在 3 次測試運行中，一個簡單的 DIY 抓取器收到了 26 個區塊頁面。封鎖頁面是商店封鎖請求時顯示的內容，例如沃爾瑪的「機器人還是人類？」頁面或亞馬遜的「繼續購物」頁面。該模型對所有 26 個答案都回答“無價格”。這些答案很誠實，但用戶仍然沒有得到價格。每一個明顯錯誤
